what_happened: In job 80vv, the user corrected Athena's first reading before work began. The job gives the planner and critic a view of git history in their planning snapshot. The first reading planned to build a git repository or rewrite history inside the snapshot and to widen the planner and critic grants. The user replaced this with a simpler design. At snapshot time, plain git log writes a generated history file covering the last 200 commits on the base, with subject, date and changed paths. The file leaves out records/ and private paths. Both briefs name the file and say what it holds, and the agents read it with Read and Grep. The user also asked for tests that the file is written, that it excludes records/, and that both briefs name it. The user asked for a measurement of the snapshot time it adds.
cause: The reading stage turns the request into a design without a rule to prefer the least privileged and cheapest mechanism that the agents' existing tools can use. It does not check the choice against the sandbox's permission model or the privacy exclusions, such as records/ and private paths. It also does not require a test per exclusion or a cost measurement. So a reading can pick a mechanism that widens grants or rewrites state, and only the user knows to reject it. Other classes cover wrong scope, wrong test location and missing prior state. None covers choosing an over-powered design for the stated need.
prevention: Add a default to the reading stage. When a request gives agents new information, the reading must first propose the least privileged option: a generated read-only file, named in the agent briefs, read with existing tools. It may widen grants or build repo state only with a stated reason why that option cannot work. The reading must also list what the file excludes (records/, private paths), include a test for each exclusion and for the briefs naming the file, and include a measurement of added time. A critic check should reject readings that widen agent grants without that reason.
proposed_request: Give the planner and critic a view of recent git history in their planning snapshot, without building a git repository or rewriting history in the snapshot and without widening the planner or critic grants. At snapshot time, write a generated history file produced by plain git log: the last 200 commits on the base, each with subject, date and changed paths. Exclude records/ and private paths. Tell the planner and critic in their briefs that the file exists and what it holds. They read it with Read and Grep. Acceptance: a test shows the file is written; a test shows it excludes records/ and private paths; a test shows both briefs name the file and describe its contents; the snapshot time the file adds is measured and reported.
